analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (head lines 757-765): it adds a documentation paragraph on streamed `auto` tool-call chunks, where `choices[].delta.tool_calls` entries share one `index`, the first chunk carries `id`, `type`, `function.name` and an empty `function.arguments`, and later chunks carry argument fragments that consumers concatenate. No code, wire schema, key handling, authorization, attestation or encryption behavior changes. The base units supplied (lines 1-583) are unchanged context: App Attest endpoint resumption, the drain barrier, registration fields and telemetry. They remain consistent with the existing threat model (TB-002, TB-011, T-053, T-008). The new paragraph describes plaintext SSE delta content, which is carried inside the existing `encrypted_data` envelope when E2E encryption is active, and it does not alter the fail-closed encryption rules (T-008). It does not touch the prefix-cache or SSD storage surface (T-041). The doc cites `libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMServer/Runtime/MLXOpenAIService.swift` (`streamChatCompletionFrames`) and `../architecture/inference.md#streamed-auto-tool-calls`, neither of which was supplied. Whether the provider's streaming implementation, including any tool-call handling or buffering, behaves as described, and whether chunks stay encrypted, is therefore unverified here. That is a documentation-accuracy question for the corresponding code PR, not a security regression from this change. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption was identified.
